horserace.title: WY is single-step maxT (not step-down) over raw F-stats with heterogeneous numerator df
horserace.claim_or_code: Paper: 'We apply the Westfall-Young step-down permutation procedure.' Code: max_F_perm[p] = max(perm_F) over all 30 cells each permutation; p_adj = mean(max_F_perm >= f_obs) for every cell against the same single max distribution.
horserace.problem: Two issues. (a) This is single-step maxT, not the step-down (sequential max-set shrinking) procedure the paper names; single-step is uniformly more conservative and is mislabeled. (b) More seriously, the maxT is taken over RAW F-statistics whose numerator degrees of freedom differ across cells: 1 for scalar substrates, 4 for the climate bundle, 8 for the functional-allele bundle. F-statistics with different numerator df are not on a common scale (an F with 8 restrictions has a very different null distribution than one with 1), so the per-permutation max is dominated by the low-df scalar cells and the high-df bundle cells are effectively under-tested. Every surviving cell is a scalar substrate; the 8-df functional bundle never survives (best p_adj_wy=0.066 on GDPpc). WY/maxT validity requires comparable statistics — the canonical fix is minP (max over -log p) or standardized statistics.
horserace.evidence: robustness_battery.py:241 'max_F_perm[p] = max(perm_F)'; :248 'p_adj = float(np.mean(max_F_perm >= f_obs))'. Verified df heterogeneity: climate cell num_df=4 (n=194), functional cell num_df=8 (n=154), scalar cell num_df=1 (n=194). f_test is classical OLS (line 100), not HC3, unlike the headline coef table (exercise1_shapley.py:89 cov_type='HC3').
horserace.why_it_matters: The multiplicity correction is the paper's claimed guarantee that the temporal-partition pattern is 'a statistically defensible structure rather than ... multiply-tested individual cells.' If the family statistic is on an incomparable scale, the adjusted p-values are not interpretable as a valid FWER and the choice of which substrate 'wins' a cell is biased toward low-df scalars — exactly the cells that survive. This plausibly explains why the headline 'functional bundle dominates GDPpc' does NOT survive its own WY test.
horserace.suggested_fix: Use minP (convert each F to a p-value via its own F(df_num, df_den) reference, take min p across cells per permutation) or studentize. Either relabel as single-step maxT or implement the genuine step-down algorithm. Use HC3 F-tests to match the coefficient table.

verdict.reasoning:
I re-opened robustness_battery.py and the reproduced output parquet and confirmed every load-bearing element of the finding.

(1) Single-step maxT, mislabeled "step-down". Lines 230-248 of robustness_battery.py implement: rng once at line 230; for each of n_perm permutations, perm_F is collected across all cells and `max_F_perm[p] = max(perm_F)` (line 241); then for every cell `p_adj = float(np.mean(max_F_perm >= f_obs))` (line 248). This is the single-step maxT procedure — one fixed maximum taken over the entire family, the same null max-distribution used for every hypothesis. There is no sequential shrinking of the max-set after a rejection. The paper at horserace.tex:298 calls it "the Westfall-Young step-down permutation procedure." So the label is wrong; single-step maxT is uniformly (weakly) more conservative than step-down maxT. Confirmed as stated.

(2) maxT over RAW F with heterogeneous numerator df — the serious issue. The F-test in _joint_f_stat (lines 90-101) sets the R matrix to len(substrate_cols) rows, so numerator df = number of substrate columns. I verified empirically on log_gdppc_2015: climate_bundle num_df=4 (n=161), functional_alleles num_df=8 (n=154), every scalar num_df=1. The per-permutation maximum at line 241 is taken over these raw F's with incomparable null distributions. Quantitatively: with denom df~145, E[F]≈1.0 for all, but the right tail is far heavier for low df — a per-cell p=0.001 event is raw F=11.28 for 1 df but only F=3.50 for 8 df. The single per-perm max is therefore dominated by the fat-tailed 1-df scalar cells, holding the 8-df functional bundle to an inappropriately high raw-F bar relative to its own null. This is exactly the WY/maxT validity condition the reviewer cites (statistics must be on a common scale; canonical fix is minP or standardized statistics).

(3) The consequence the reviewer predicts is borne out in the reproduced output. All five survivors at p_adj_wy<0.05 are num_df=1 scalar substrates (ancestral_yield_log on log_popd_1500 p=0.002, log_popd_2025 p=0.030, log_pop_growth p=0.000; neolithic_frac on log_popd_2025 p=0.000, dt_timing_year p=0.005). The 8-df functional_alleles bundle never survives; its best is exactly p_adj_wy=0.066 on log_gdppc_2015 (F=8.46), as the reviewer stated. On its own 8-df scale F=8.46 is per-cell p≈4e-7 — extraordinarily significant — yet it is buried by the maxT.

(4) Classical-vs-HC3 mismatch confirmed. _joint_f_stat line 92 is plain sm.OLS(...).fit() (no cov_type), whereas the headline coefficient table exercise1_shapley.py:89 uses .fit(cov_type='HC3'). For the functional bundle on GDPpc this matters: F_classical=8.46 vs F_HC3=10.93.

Two refinements that do not weaken the finding: (a) the family is 30 cells (5 substrates x 6 outcomes per _substrate_cells and OUTCOMES), not 24 — the paper itself is internally inconsistent (line 298 says 24; lines 51/55 say "thirty"), and the reviewer's own evidence count was illustrative. (b) Separately, the paper text at line 298 names the GDPpc/pop-growth survivors as "Predicted heterozygosity" with F=11.33 and 10.82, neither of which appears anywhere in the reproduced output (the actual survivors are ancestral_yield_log and neolithic_frac) — a text-vs-code mismatch beyond this finding's scope but reinforcing that the WY results are not interpretable as reported. The core methodological defect — single-step maxT mislabeled step-down, taken over raw F's with df 1/4/8 on incomparable scales, biasing survival toward low-df scalars and under-testing the high-df bundle — is fully verified and the "why it matters" (the FWER guarantee is not valid and the headline functional-bundle-dominates-GDPpc result fails its own test for a mechanical, not substantive, reason) holds.

Severity: major is appropriate. The multiplicity correction is the paper's explicit claim of statistical defensibility for the temporal-partition pattern, and the test as coded does not deliver a valid FWER across heterogeneous-df cells.

horserace.title: Shapley dominance rankings reported as definite but have no CIs and are within sampling noise
horserace.location: shapley.py:41-46 (raw rsquared, no bootstrap), exercise1_shapley.py:185-217 (no CI output); claims at horserace.tex:49,216-222
horserace.claim_or_code: Shapley shares are computed once on the point sample using res.rsquared with no resampling; the paper presents a clean 'temporal partition' with a definite dominant substrate per outcome (lines 49, 216-222). No confidence intervals are reported anywhere for the Shapley shares.

A nonparametric bootstrap over the 162 complete-case countries (300 draws) gives 95% difference-CIs that straddle zero for the contested rankings: density-2025 functional minus neolithic = [-0.048, +0.134] (P(neolithic>=functional)=0.19); growth functional minus ancestral = [-0.155, +0.120] (P=0.46, effectively a tie); density-1500 climate minus functional = [-0.024, +0.123] (P(functional>=climate)=0.08). None of the headline 'dominance' margins is statistically distinguishable from its runner-up.
horserace.evidence: shapley.py:45-46 returns float(res.rsquared) (no adjustment, no resampling). exercise1_shapley.py main() emits only point shapley_r2. Bootstrap I ran (300 draws, complete-case n=162) produced the difference-CIs quoted above.
horserace.why_it_matters: The entire 'each chapter has its protagonist' thesis (line 49) rests on dominance orderings that are not statistically separable. Without CIs the reader cannot see that the partition is within noise; the paper presents coin-flip-level orderings as established structure.
horserace.suggested_fix: Bootstrap the Shapley shares over countries and report per-cell CIs and, for the dominance claims, the bootstrap probability that the named substrate actually has the largest share. Soften 'dominates' to 'is the point-estimate leader, not statistically separable from X' where CIs overlap.

verdict.reasoning:
CODE CLAIMS — all verified. shapley.py:41-46 (_r2) returns raw float(res.rsquared) with no adjustment and no resampling; exercise1_shapley.py main() (185-217) writes only point shapley_r2/baseline_r2/full_model_r2 to parquet, no CI. The Westfall-Young correction that the paper touts (horserace.tex:51,295-298) is applied to the MEDIATION regression F-statistics (24 cells), NOT to the Shapley R^2 shares — so the dominance orderings genuinely carry no propagated uncertainty. The only sample variation on the shares anywhere is point-estimate subsample/leave-one-out perturbation in robustness_battery.py, never a difference-CI. So the reviewer's central technical assertion is correct.

BOOTSTRAP — reproduces. I ran a nonparametric country bootstrap (300 draws) on the complete-case panel (n=162 for early outcomes, matching the stored n_obs). My difference-CIs land within draw-noise of the reviewer's: density-2025 functional-minus-neolithic [-0.037,+0.122], P(neolithic>=functional)=0.14 (reviewer: [-0.048,+0.134], P=0.19); growth functional-minus-ancestral [-0.152,+0.122], P=0.47 (reviewer: [-0.155,+0.120], P=0.46, effectively a dead heat — point margin is 0.0962 vs 0.0957); density-1500 climate-minus-functional [-0.013,+0.121], P(functional>=climate)=0.04. These three contested orderings do straddle/nearly-straddle zero, confirming that part.

WHERE THE FINDING IS OVERSTATED. The blanket claim 'None of the headline dominance margins is statistically distinguishable from its runner-up' is FALSE. I bootstrapped the two marquee cells and both are robustly separable: functional dominates gdppc_2015 over its runner-up, CI [+0.090,+0.255], P(runner-up wins)=0.00 (margin 0.16); functional dominates dt_timing over neolithic, CI [+0.040,+0.158], P=0.00 (margin 0.09). These are precisely the paper's headline 'functional-allele bundle dominates per-capita income and DT timing' claims (lines 49,218) and they survive. Also, the paper is partly candid: line 216 explicitly labels the growth cell 'a near-tie with the functional bundle (0.096).' So the partition is NOT uniformly coin-flip — roughly half the headline cells (gdppc, dt_timing, density-1500) are separable and half (density-2025, growth, urban-change) are within noise.

SEPARATE FACTUAL BUG I NOTICED. The reproduced parquet shows functional_alleles=0.0641 > neolithic_frac=0.0390 on log_popd_2025, yet horserace.tex:220 asserts neolithic is 'the largest substrate contribution on this outcome.' That is a text-vs-data inconsistency (the stated 2025 'protagonist' is wrong against the current results) — a distinct issue from the missing-CI point.

NET: the methodological gap (Shapley shares are estimated random variables with no uncertainty quantification; several contested orderings are within sampling noise) is real and worth a remedy — adding difference-CIs would let readers see which cells of the partition are separable. But the finding's framing that the ENTIRE thesis rests on indistinguishable orderings is refuted by the two large-margin headline cells that bootstrap cleanly, and the growth tie is already disclosed. The fix is presentational (report difference-CIs), not result-overturning, so the severity is below 'major.'
verdict.correction: The Shapley shares indeed carry no propagated uncertainty (shapley.py:45-46 raw rsquared; exercise1_shapley.py emits point estimates only), and the bootstrap difference-CIs for the density-2025, growth-1950-2025, and density-1500 cells do straddle/nearly-straddle zero, so those specific orderings are within sampling noise and should not be stated as definite. HOWEVER the finding's universal claim that NO headline dominance margin is separable is wrong: the functional bundle's dominance on log GDPpc 2015 (difference-CI [+0.090,+0.255], P=0.00) and on DT timing (difference-CI [+0.040,+0.158], P=0.00) are robustly distinguishable, and the paper already discloses the growth cell as 'a near-tie' (line 216). The remedy is to report difference-CIs alongside the Shapley table (flagging the within-noise cells), not to retract the partition. Separately, horserace.tex:220 misstates the density-2025 protagonist: the reproduced data has functional_alleles (0.064) above neolithic_frac (0.039), so 'the largest substrate contribution on this outcome' is factually incorrect and should be corrected regardless of the CI issue.

The function `_r2` is the only R² primitive; it is called for the baseline, every coalition subset (line 90), the full model (line 92), and every Shapley marginal increment is the difference of two such raw R² values (line 100). No adjusted R², no penalty for column count.

GREP: no adjusted/cross-validation/out-of-sample/overfit/dimensionality terms in paper5_horserace/*.py (excluding tests) — the only "adjusted" hits are unrelated ancestry-adjusted data builds. horserace.tex never mentions adjusted-R², OOS, or coalition-player dimensionality.

MECHANISM (placebo I ran, n=118, dt_timing_year, 2000 reps): pure-noise regressors mechanically inflate raw R² over the controls baseline by +0.0037 (1 col, scalar), +0.0155 (4 cols, climate), +0.0305 (8 cols, functional) — i.e. ~K/(n-p), ~8x larger for the 8-column functional bundle than for a scalar substrate. I reproduced the n's from the committed parquets: Shapley log_popd_1500 n=162 (all six Shapley outcomes 118-162); WY ancestral_yield_log x log_popd_1500 n=194, neolithic cells n=175, functional cells n=162. So the ~32-country gap and the reviewer's "approx 40 countries" / n=162 vs n=194 numbers are essentially right.

The "why it matters" framing is overstated, however. (1) The Shapley (unique-variance dominance) and the WY F-test are TWO distinct exercises, not one matrix on one sample: the WY runs on the mediation regression (substrate + pathway dummies + geography), testing joint coefficient significance (sec 5, line 298), while the Shapley is a variance decomposition. The paper never asserts they share a row-set. (2) The differing samples are standard, required listwise behavior: the Shapley MUST use a common sample so the decomposition identity (sum phi = R2_full - R2_baseline) holds and substrates stay comparable; per-cell WY listwise is the conventional way to maximize power per significance test. Even within the WY table the cells already run on different n (functional cells 162 vs ancestral 194) — intrinsic to listwise deletion, not a defect. (3) The paper discloses the sample: line 81 "162 with non-missing values on all five substrates," line 560 "N approx 162 on the full five-substrate panel," and the full-OLS table reports per-outcome N (118-162). There is no concealed claim of a common sample, so the alleged harm (incoherent matrix / undermined FWER defense) does not follow.

verdict.correction: The factual observation is correct (joint-listwise Shapley n=162 vs per-cell WY n=175-194, driven by functional-allele missingness), but the consequence is overstated. The Shapley dominance table and the Westfall-Young F-test are two distinct statistical objects, not "a single coherent matrix": joint-listwise is required for the Shapley decomposition identity and per-cell listwise is standard for maximizing each significance test's power. The differing samples are disclosed (lines 81, 560, plus per-outcome N in the OLS table) and are normal listwise practice, not a defect; the FWER procedure is correctly applied per cell. The only legitimate residual is a presentational nicety: the paper could add one sentence flagging that the dominance and significance calls use slightly different country sets. This is a transparency suggestion, not a methodological error, so the substantive-harm claim is essentially refuted while the underlying numbers stand.

On the Shapley-R2 metric (the paper's principal decomposition), the largest substrate per outcome is: logD_1500=climate, logD_2025=functional, pop growth=functional, urban change=climate, GDPpc=functional, DT timing=functional. Ancestral crop yield is the largest Shapley contributor on ZERO of six outcomes (max 0.096 on pop growth, a near-tie that LOSES to functional 0.0962 vs 0.0957); Neolithic fraction is largest on ZERO outcomes (0.039 on logD_2025 loses to functional 0.064; 0.032 on DT timing loses to functional 0.122). The ancestral-yield and Neolithic 'dominance' claims rest ONLY on the WY joint-F survivors — but on that same WY metric the climate and functional 'dominance' claims FAIL (climate's largest F is 2.14; functional/GDPpc F=8.46 non-significant). horserace.why_it_matters: The 'each witness speaks for its own epoch' temporal partition is the paper's central substantive contribution (abstract, intro, discussion, conclusion all build on it). If it requires silently changing the success metric per cell, it is a post-hoc narrative imposed on multiply-tested cells, exactly the failure mode the prior internal analysis flagged ('Shapley dominance — ancestral crop yield wins 3 of 4' is contradicted: it wins 0 of 6 on Shapley).
horserace.suggested_fix: State explicitly that two distinct criteria are in play (Shapley unique-variance share vs FWER-robust joint-F), report both for every headline cell, and reframe: climate and functional bundle have the largest Shapley shares on their cells but are not FWER-robust; ancestral yield and Neolithic fraction are FWER-robust but never the largest Shapley share. Drop the unqualified verb 'dominates' or define it precisely per claim.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced every number the reviewer cites from the two named files. exercise1_shapley_results.parquet (5-substrate panel): Shapley idxmax per outcome is climate_bundle(log_popd_1500=0.0875), functional_alleles(log_popd_2025=0.0641), functional_alleles(pop_growth=0.0962 vs ancestral 0.0957 — a near-tie functional barely wins), climate_bundle(urban=0.0759), functional_alleles(gdppc=0.1745), functional_alleles(dt_timing=0.1219). ancestral_yield_log is Shapley-top on 0/6 (max 0.0957, rank 2 on growth and gdppc) and neolithic_frac is Shapley-top on 0/6 (rank 2 on density-2025 and dt). All exact. robustness_battery.parquet (check==wy_correction): the only cells with p_adj_wy<0.05 are ancestral_yield on {popd_1500 F=15.5, popd_2025 F=10.4 p=0.030, pop_growth F=27.0} and neolithic_frac on {popd_2025 F=17.9, dt_timing F=13.2}. climate_bundle's max F is 2.14 (urban, p=0.975) — never significant; functional_alleles max F is 8.46 (gdppc, p=0.066) — never significant. All exact.

The reviewer's STRUCTURAL claim is therefore TRUE and verified: no single metric yields the headline 'temporal partition.' On Shapley alone the per-outcome winners are climate/functional/functional/climate/functional/functional — ancestral and Neolithic win nothing, and climate 'dominates' only density-1500/urban. On WY alone the survivors are ancestral and Neolithic — climate and functional survive nothing. So the four pillars of the partition rest on two non-coincident criteria: climate→density-1500 and functional→GDPpc are Shapley-based (and FAIL WY), while ancestral→growth/density and Neolithic→density-2025/dt are WY-based (and LOSE on Shapley, where functional is top on those very cells). Most starkly, on density-2025 functional is Shapley-top (0.0641, but WY p=0.692) while Neolithic is WY-top (F=17.9, p<0.001, but only Shapley-2nd) — yet the abstract calls functional's GDPpc result and Neolithic's density-2025 result both 'dominates,' papering over the metric switch.

However the reviewer's 'WITHOUT DISCLOSING' charge is OVERSTATED. The paper does flag the metric basis in places: line 299 states 'The climate-bundle mediation cells do not survive FWER correction in any outcome, with the largest F-statistic at 2.14' and 'The climate channel is identified through its joint Shapley R2 contribution and its pathway-mediation share, not through a direct post-pathway coefficient' (repeated line 552). The intro (line 49) deliberately differentiates wording: ancestral 'carries the largest joint statistic on convergence-window population growth' (the F/WY metric) vs functional 'carries the largest variance contribution on per-capita income' (the Shapley metric). So the criterion-switch is partially disclosed in the body, not silently hidden — contrary to the reviewer's framing. What IS fair: the abstract (line 29) and conclusion (line 565) flatten these into uniform 'dominates'/'predicts' verbs that obscure which cell rests on which metric.

I also found a separate corroborating defect the reviewer did not name: the paper's own WY narrative (line 298) is STALE. It reports the two non-ancestral survivors as 'predicted heterozygosity' on {GDPpc F=11.33 p=0.015, pop_growth F=10.82 p=0.019} — but the current data file assigns those two survivor slots to neolithic_frac on {density-2025, dt_timing} with different F-values, and quotes ancestral density-2025 as p=0.022 vs data 0.030. The text describes an older heterozygosity-based 4-substrate matrix while the data is the updated 5-substrate (functional/neolithic) matrix. This makes the metric basis even murkier than the reviewer realized, but it is a text-vs-data drift, not the metric-switching the reviewer alleged.

Net: the reviewer's evidence is accurate and the structural concern (headline partition holds under no single criterion; ancestral/Neolithic win 0/6 on Shapley, contradicting the older internal 'wins 3 of 4 on Shapley' note) is real and bears on the paper's central contribution. But it is not undisclosed fabrication — the body signposts the dual-metric structure — so it is a major framing/inference problem, not a blocker.
verdict.correction: The partition is genuinely supported by two non-coincident criteria rather than one: climate→density-1500 and functional→GDPpc rest on the Shapley-R2 metric (both fail WY: climate max F=2.14, functional gdppc F=8.46 p=0.066), while ancestral→growth/density and Neolithic→density-2025/dt rest on the WY joint-F survivors (both lose on Shapley, where functional is top on those cells; ancestral and Neolithic are Shapley-top on 0/6). This is real and the abstract/conclusion use a uniform 'dominates' verb that blurs the metric switch. But the reviewer's 'without disclosing' charge is overstated: the body explicitly states climate is identified by Shapley+mediation and not WY (lines 299, 552) and the intro differentiates 'largest joint statistic' (F-based) from 'largest variance contribution' (Shapley-based) (line 49). The defensible characterization is: the headline temporal partition is assembled from two metrics whose winners do not coincide, and while the body signposts this, the abstract and conclusion present it under uniform dominance language without flagging the per-cell criterion. Separately, the WY subsection text (line 298) is stale relative to the data file — it attributes two survivors to 'predicted heterozygosity' (GDPpc, growth) when the current data attributes them to neolithic_frac (density-2025, dt_timing) and gives ancestral density-2025 as p=0.022 vs data 0.030.

The 'suppressor structure' is NOT confined to the heterozygosity and pandemic rows — it pervades the climate, functional, Neolithic, and ancestral-yield rows too (climate/logD_2025=0.17 with CI [-1.60,0.74] crossing 0; climate/GDPpc=-0.92; functional/logD_1500=0.12 CI [-1.63,0.65]; Neolithic on 5 of 6 cells). horserace.why_it_matters: Pathway-mediation is the mechanism story for the climate channel and is invoked in the discussion/conclusion as the identification strategy ('the climate channel is identified specifically through pathway mediation'). verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced all three headline statistics exactly from exercise2_mediation_results.parquet (30 rows = 5 substrates x 6 outcomes): (1) point in [0,1] AND CI contained in [0,1] = 5/30; (2) point estimate outside [0,1] = 11/30; (3) CI crosses 0 or 1 = 25/30. Every cited example matches to 3 decimals: climate_bundle/log_popd_2025 = 0.166 CI[-1.601,0.738]; climate_bundle/log_gdppc_2015 = -0.918 CI[-4.306,0.733]; pandemic/log_pop_growth = 5.585 CI[-43.454,39.382]; functional/log_popd_1500 = 0.120 CI[-1.634,0.652]; pandemic/urban = -2.155.

The caption-vs-table contradiction is REAL. That cell's CI is [-1.60,0.74] (crosses 0), and tab05_mediation_table.tex line 8 does NOT bold it, while the table footnote defines bolding as 'point estimate in [0,1] with CI nearly contained.' So the caption contradicts the table on this cell.

The 'suppressor concentrated in heterozygosity and pandemic rows' claim (lines 262, 279) is overstated as the reviewer says: neolithic_frac crosses 0/1 on 6/6 cells, climate_bundle/gdppc = -0.92, functional_alleles/log_popd_1500 CI crosses. Suppressor/CI-crossing structure pervades all five rows.

Mitigating facts the reviewer underweights: (a) the WY-FWER subsection (lines 298-299) explicitly concedes 'the climate-bundle mediation cells do not survive FWER correction in any outcome' and states climate is identified 'through its joint Shapley R^2 contribution and its pathway-mediation share, not through a direct post-pathway coefficient' — so the identification claim is more hedged than the finding implies. (b) Line 317 already reports baseline share-in-[0,1] = 58% (my recompute: 19/30 = 63% point-in, consistent). verdict.correction: The 5/30-clean, 11/30-outside-[0,1], 25/30-CI-crossing counts and all cited examples are correct, and the caption (line 267) does mislabel the density-2025 climate cell (0.17, CI[-1.60,0.74], unbolded in Table 5) as 'well-mediated.' However, the claim that the paper presents mediation as THE climate-identification strategy is overstated: the FWER subsection (lines 298-299) explicitly states the climate mediation cells fail FWER correction and that climate is identified via Shapley R^2 plus pathway share, not a direct post-pathway coefficient. Severity stays major for the factual caption/table contradiction and the 'concentrated in two rows' misstatement, but the 'mediation largely fails / overstates evidence' framing is partly pre-empted by the paper's own hedge. Reviewer also slightly mislabeled the heterozygosity row (it is functional_alleles in this file) and undercounted neolithic suppressor cells (6/6, not 5/6).

(4) MORE SEVERE THAN CLAIMED: the reviewer's "why it matters" (FWER p-values depend on 24 vs 30) is correct, but the actual harm is concrete factual error. The two "predicted heterozygosity" cells do not exist (no H_pred substrate in the matrix), F=11.33/10.82 appear nowhere in the data, and the best GDPpc cell (functional_alleles, F=8.46, p_adj_wy=0.066) does not survive at 0.05. horserace.title: DARC 'attenuated to insignificance' over-claim: the coefficient is already insignificant at baseline
horserace.claim_or_code: Repeated claim: DARC's negative coefficient on log GDPpc 'survives colonial-extractive-institutions and raw African-ancestry controls but is largely absorbed---a sixty-five percent attenuation, sufficient to render the coefficient insignificant---by the Bockstette-Putterman pre-colonial state-history index.'
horserace.problem: The DARC baseline coefficient is -2.645 with p=0.113 (N=154) — already insignificant at the 10% level BEFORE any partialling. A coefficient that is not significant at baseline cannot be 'rendered insignificant' by a control; the 65% attenuation moves it from -2.645 (p=0.11) to +0.94 (p=0.54). The substantive sign-flip-and-shrink is real and interesting, but the recurring phrasing 'sufficient to render the coefficient insignificant' (abstract, intro, discussion, conclusion) implies a significant baseline effect that the data do not show.
horserace.evidence: exercise_colonial_partial_extended_results.parquet: spec=baseline fa_darc beta=-2.645003 p=0.112778 N=154; spec=+state_hist fa_darc beta=+0.937833 p=0.540718. Table colonial-partial-extended (horserace.tex:487-491) reports baseline p=0.11.
horserace.why_it_matters: The DARC institutional-proxy reinterpretation is built on a single cross-sectional OLS coefficient (N=154) that is statistically indistinguishable from zero from the outset; describing it as significant-then-killed-by-state-history inflates the strength of the reinterpretation that the discussion and conclusion lean on heavily.
horserace.suggested_fix: Replace 'sufficient to render the coefficient insignificant' with an accurate description: the baseline DARC loading is already insignificant (p=0.11); conditioning on state history shrinks it by ~65% and flips its sign. Frame the channel-displacement reading as suggestive, given the modest and non-significant baseline magnitude.

verdict.reasoning: I reproduced the parquet (exercise_colonial_partial_extended_results.parquet) and the cited tex lines. The data confirm the reviewer exactly: spec=baseline fa_darc beta=-2.645003, p=0.112778, N=154 (|t|=1.59); spec=+state_hist fa_darc beta=+0.937833, p=0.540718, N=136. Baseline p=0.113 is NOT significant at the 10% level (0.113 > 0.10), so the coefficient is statistically indistinguishable from zero before any partialling. The magnitude attenuation is 64.5% (2.645 -> 0.938), matching the paper's "65%". The over-claim phrasing "sufficient to render the coefficient insignificant" appears verbatim at horserace.tex:53 (intro), :108, and :554 (discussion); line 108 says "renders it insignificant". A coefficient already insignificant at baseline cannot be "rendered insignificant" by a control — the phrasing presupposes a significant baseline the data do not show. There is genuine internal tension: Table colonial-partial-extended (line 487) honestly prints baseline p=0.11, contradicting the prose three pages over. Two corrections to the reviewer's framing: (a) of the five cited locations, lines 29 (abstract) and 565 (conclusion) do NOT contain the over-claim — they say "largely absorbed"/"imperfect proxy", which is accurate; the over-claim is confined to lines 53, 108, 554. (b) The substantive reinterpretation (sign flip, 65% attenuation, DARC-as-state-history-proxy) is real and correctly computed and does not actually depend on a significant baseline, so "inflates the strength of the reinterpretation" is mildly strong — the defect is rhetorical imprecision in three sentences, not a structural flaw. Net: the core factual claim is correct and the fix is to replace "sufficient to render the coefficient insignificant" with language like "leaves it insignificant and flips its sign" or "drives the already-imprecise negative loading to a small positive value".
verdict.correction: The over-claim is real but confined to horserace.tex:53, :108, and :554 (not :29 or :565, which use accurate "largely absorbed"/"imperfect proxy" language). Suggested fix: change "a 65 percent attenuation, sufficient to render the coefficient insignificant" to "a 65 percent attenuation that flips the sign of an already statistically insignificant baseline coefficient (baseline p=0.11)". The baseline DARC coefficient (-2.645, p=0.113, N=154) is not significant at the 10% level, so it cannot be "rendered" insignificant; Table 487 already reports this p=0.11, so the prose should match the table. The substantive channel-displacement reinterpretation (sign flip + 65% attenuation absorbed by state history) is correct and survives the rewording.

PAPER (horserace.tex, sec:wy-correction, the paragraph the reviewer cites): The text says "five cells survive at p_WY<0.05. horserace.title: Bootstrap CI seeds derived from Python hash() are non-deterministic across runs (PYTHONHASHSEED unset)
horserace.claim_or_code: seed = abs(hash((outcome, substrate_key))) % (2**31) — the bootstrap seed for each mediation cell is computed from hash() of a string tuple. mediation.py then does rng = np.random.default_rng(seed).
horserace.problem: Python string/tuple hashing is salted per process when PYTHONHASHSEED is unset (the default). I verified two fresh interpreters give 662750999 vs 1783373349 for hash(('log_gdppc_2015','functional_alleles')). No PYTHONHASHSEED is set anywhere in the repo and there is no reproduce orchestrator for paper5 (only paper4 has one). Therefore every re-run of exercise2_mediation.py, exercise2_subsample_stability.py, exercise3_climate_clusters.py, and the continent_fe / pre1900 mediation legs of robustness_battery.py draws different bootstrap samples, so the reported 95% percentile-bootstrap CIs in Table tab05_mediation_table and Figures fig04/fig05/fig06 are not reproducible. (The WY permutation at robustness_battery.py:230 uses a fixed seed=46 and is reproducible; only the hash-seeded cells are affected.)
horserace.evidence: Bash: PYTHONHASHSEED 'NOT SET'; python3 -c hash(...) run twice -> 662750999 then 1783373349. grep found hash()-seed usage in 5 locations and no PYTHONHASHSEED anywhere under analysis/.
horserace.why_it_matters: Bootstrap CIs are reported to two-to-three decimals in the paper and used to bold 'clean' mediation cells; a referee re-running the code will not reproduce the exact CIs, and with n_boot=500-1000 on heavily heavy-tailed shares (some CIs span [-43,39]) the bounds can move materially. The point estimates are deterministic, but the inference is not.
horserace.suggested_fix: Replace abs(hash((...))) with a deterministic hash (e.g., int(hashlib.sha256(repr(key).encode()).hexdigest(),16) % (2**31)) or assign explicit integer seeds per (outcome,substrate) cell, and/or export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in a paper5 reproduce script. Re-generate the affected parquets/figures/tables.

verdict.reasoning: All claims verified against source. (1) PYTHONHASHSEED is NOT SET in the environment and grep -rn over /Volumes/BIGDATA/HYDE35/analysis/ returns zero matches. (2) All five cited hash-seed lines exist verbatim: exercise2_mediation.py:49 (abs(hash((outcome, substrate_key)))%2**31, n_boot=1000); exercise2_subsample_stability.py:63 ((44+abs(hash((stage,outcome,substrate_key))))%2**31, n_boot=500); exercise3_climate_clusters.py:57 (abs(hash((outcome,skey,'hyde')))%2**31, n_boot=1000); robustness_battery.py:123 (continent_fe) and :359 (pre1900_mediation, n_boot=300). (3) Hash non-determinism reproduced: two fresh python3 interpreters gave abs(hash(('log_gdppc_2015','functional_alleles')))%2**31 = 1578461975 vs 425998078 (reviewer cited the raw hash form; same per-process-salt phenomenon). (4) Mechanism confirmed in mediation.py lines 53 and 94: point = _share(df) is computed once before any draw (so point estimates and beta/R2 ARE deterministic, as the reviewer concedes), then rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) drives rng.integers(0,n,n) resampling; the percentile CI (np.quantile at alpha/2, 1-alpha/2) depends entirely on the hash-salted seed. (5) WY permutation at robustness_battery.py:230 uses fixed np.random.default_rng(46) and is reproducible, exactly as the reviewer scoped. (6) paper5_horserace has no reproduce orchestrator (paper4 has run_all.py/run_pre1500_volcanic.py); neither exports PYTHONHASHSEED. (7) Paper impact confirmed: tab05_mediation_table.tex reports CIs to two decimals and bolds cells by whether the bootstrap CI is 'nearly contained' in [0,1]; some CIs are extremely heavy-tailed (e.g. pre-1500 pandemic 5.58 [-43.45, 39.38]), and horserace.tex:258/266 confirm '1,000 country resamples / 95% percentile-bootstrap CIs'. horserace.title: Ancestral crop yield called 'dominant predictor across the demographic-density trajectory' but dominates no Shapley cell outright (ties growth, second on density 1500, near-zero on density 2025)

horserace.title: Westfall-Young F-statistic uses homoskedastic OLS SEs while the headline OLS table uses HC3; minor dead-code hypotheses string
horserace.claim_or_code: robustness_battery.py:92 'res = sm.OLS(d[y_col], X).fit()' then res.f_test(R) — classical (homoskedastic) F-test. exercise1_shapley.py:89 uses .fit(cov_type="HC3"). Line 94 builds a 'hypotheses' string that is never used (the R contrast matrix is used instead).

Cross-country data are typically heteroskedastic, so the F-stats (and the survivor set at the 0.05 boundary, e.g. density 2025 ancestral yield at p=0.030) could shift under HC3. The dead 'hypotheses' string at line 94 is harmless but is leftover scaffolding.

horserace.why_it_matters: The WY permutation distribution is internally consistent (observed and permuted F use the same homoskedastic estimator), so the procedure is valid; but the reported significance is not robust to heteroskedasticity, and the boundary survivor (p=0.030) could be sensitive. Low-to-moderate impact.
horserace.suggested_fix: Either compute the F-stat with the same HC3 covariance as the OLS table (res = ...fit(cov_type='HC3'); res.f_test(R)) consistently for observed and permuted draws, or add a sentence noting the WY F-test is homoskedastic by design. Delete the unused 'hypotheses' string at line 94.

I opened both cited files. The two technical claims hold exactly: robustness_battery.py:92 uses plain homoskedastic OLS (`sm.OLS(d[y_col], X).fit()`), and the WY procedure (check_wy_correction, lines 204-261) computes BOTH observed F (line 222) and permuted F (line 239) through the same `_joint_f_stat` helper. So the WY/FWER F-statistics are indeed homoskedastic, while the headline OLS table at exercise1_shapley.py:89 uses `.fit(cov_type="HC3")`. The dead-code claim is also correct: line 94 assigns `hypotheses` but line 100 uses a manually built R matrix in `res.f_test(R)`, so the string is unused leftover scaffolding. Harmless.

However, two things weaken the finding. (1) The reviewer's flagship piece of evidence is wrong: the cited boundary survivor "density 2025 ancestral yield at p=0.030" does not exist. horserace.tex:298 reports that exact cell at p_WY=0.022 (F=10.40), and no p=0.030 appears anywhere in the survivor set (the five survivors are p<0.001, 0.002, 0.015, 0.019, 0.022). The closest-to-boundary survivor is 0.022, with more margin than the fabricated 0.030. (2) The reviewer correctly concedes the WY procedure is internally valid (observed and permuted statistics use the same estimator), so the FWER inference is exact under the sharp permutation null regardless of heteroskedasticity. The legitimate residual concern is only a convention mismatch (homoskedastic F in the FWER test vs HC3 in the descriptive table) and a "could shift" worry that rests on a misquoted p-value. This is a real but cosmetic/consistency nit, not an error that affects reported conclusions.
verdict.correction: The two code observations are accurate (homoskedastic OLS in the WY F-stat at robustness_battery.py:92; HC3 in the OLS table at exercise1_shapley.py:89; unused `hypotheses` string at line 94). But the boundary-survivor evidence is incorrect: the density-2025 ancestral-yield cell is reported at p_WY=0.022 (horserace.tex:298), not p=0.030; no p=0.030 cell exists. The WY permutation procedure is internally consistent and the FWER inference is valid as run, so this is a convention/style mismatch plus harmless dead code, with the specific "could shift at the 0.030 boundary" sensitivity argument resting on a misquoted number. Severity remains minor.

horserace.title: Bootstrap seeds from unsalted hash() are non-reproducible across runs; every published mediation CI changes run-to-run
horserace.problem: Bootstrap RNG seeds are computed as `seed = abs(hash((outcome, substrate_key))) % (2**31)` and passed into mediation_share_*_with_ci. Python salts str/tuple-of-str hashing via PYTHONHASHSEED, which is unset anywhere in the repo, so the seed (and thus every bootstrap CI) differs on each process invocation. Point estimates are stable (full-data) but the published CIs cannot be regenerated.
horserace.evidence: grep found the abs(hash(...)) pattern at those lines and found no PYTHONHASHSEED setting in any .py. Demonstrated non-determinism: two consecutive `python3 -c "print(abs(hash(('log_gdppc_2015','functional_alleles'))) % (2**31))"` calls returned 1550097164 then 2093806037. exercise2_mediation_results.parquet stores CIs such as log_gdppc_2015~climate_bundle ci_lower=-4.306 ci_upper=0.733 that depend on this seed.
horserace.why_it_matters: The paper reports mediation shares with bootstrap CIs (line 262) and figures derived from them. With per-process-random seeds the committed parquet cannot be reproduced and every reported interval and n_boot_valid count is run-dependent. (The WY permutation rng=46 and LOO seed=0 are correctly fixed; only the bootstrap-CI cells are affected.)
horserace.suggested_fix: Replace hash-based seeds with a deterministic mapping (explicit dict of (outcome,substrate)->int, or zlib.crc32(key.encode())), or export a fixed PYTHONHASHSEED and document it; then re-run exercise2/robustness and re-commit parquets + figures.

verdict.reasoning: Every cited line exists exactly as quoted and the mechanism is real. exercise2_mediation.py:49 = `seed = abs(hash((outcome, substrate_key))) % (2**31)`; robustness_battery.py:123 = `abs(hash(("continent_fe", outcome, skey)))`; robustness_battery.py:359 = `abs(hash(("pre1900_mediation", outcome, skey)))`; exercise3_climate_clusters.py:57 = `abs(hash((outcome, skey, "hyde")))`; exercise2_subsample_stability.py:63 = `(44 + abs(hash((stage, outcome, substrate_key))))`. All inputs are tuples of strings (Python salts these via PYTHONHASHSEED) and the seed is passed straight into mediation_share_with_ci / mediation_share_partial_r2_with_ci, both of which build `np.random.default_rng(seed)` (mediation.py:66, :116) to drive the bootstrap index draws. `grep` confirms PYTHONHASHSEED is set nowhere in analysis/ and is UNSET in the live env; the only orchestrator (.sh) is a long_shadow file unrelated to paper5. I reproduced the non-determinism: three process invocations of `hash(('log_gdppc_2015','functional_alleles'))%2**31` gave 393582455, 2047659967, 2017679891. Re-running the exact cited cell (log_gdppc_2015~climate_bundle, n_boot=1000) under those three seeds yielded CIs [-4.599,0.759], [-4.664,0.750], [-4.441,0.790] — all differing from each other and from the committed parquet [-4.306,0.733]. The parquet also stores n_boot_valid=999 for that cell (vs 1000 elsewhere), exactly the run-dependent count the reviewer flags. The reviewer's scoping caveat is also correct: WY rng=46 (robustness_battery.py:230) and LOO seed=0 (lines 173/179) are genuinely fixed; only the bootstrap-CI seeds are hash-derived. So the literal technical claim — committed CIs are non-reproducible across runs — is fully confirmed. I downgrade severity to minor only because impact is reproducibility-only: every point estimate (0.75/0.92/0.24/0.29 headline shares) is full-data and seed-independent, the CIs vary only at the ~0.1 level in the tails without crossing any interpretive threshold (the GDP cell is a wide zero-crossing suppressor cell under every seed), and the inferential backbone (Westfall-Young FWER, five surviving cells) uses the fixed rng=46 and is untouched. No number a reader would cite changes meaningfully; the defect is a real but easily-fixed reproducibility hole (set PYTHONHASHSEED or replace hash() with a stable hash such as hashlib).

horserace.title: Paper and code oscillate between '5 substrate / 30 cell / 5!=120' and stale '4 substrate / 24 cell / 16 cell / 4x6' framings
horserace.location: horserace.tex:51,55,408 vs 262,289,298,527; robustness_battery.py:5-9 docstring; figA_robustness_battery.py:5 docstring
horserace.problem: The abstract/intro/H-pred sections describe 'thirty substrate-by-outcome tests' and 'all 5!=120 substrate orderings', but the results/robustness sections say 'With 24 substrate-by-outcome mediation cells' (298), '4-substrate-by-6-outcome mediation matrix' (262, fig caption 289), 'the ranking of substrates across the 24 cells' and 'the 16 cells'/'4x4 horserace' (527). The code actually runs 5 substrates x 6 outcomes = 30 cells, and the WY permutation maximises over all 30. So the multiple-testing denominator stated in section 298 (24) contradicts the code.
horserace.evidence: Committed parquets confirm 30 rows each and 5 substrates: exercise1_shapley_results substrates=[ancestral_yield_log, climate_bundle, functional_alleles, neolithic_frac, pandemic_intensity_norm], n cells=30; exercise2_mediation 30; robustness wy_correction 30. robustness_battery.py:5-9 docstring still reads 'All checks run on the 4-substrate x 6-outcome matrix: climate bundle, H_pred_pwadj, ancestral_yield_log, pandemic_intensity_norm' while SUBSTRATES_FOR_SHAPLEY at line 47 is the 5-substrate set. figA_robustness_battery.py:5 docstring says '4-substrate x 4-outcome heatmap'.
horserace.why_it_matters: A reader cannot tell over how many tests the FWER correction is performed (its denominator), which is load-bearing for the WY claim; the 24-vs-30 discrepancy directly affects the stated correction. The stale docstrings (which even list H_pred as a substrate) would mislead anyone reproducing or extending the battery.
horserace.suggested_fix: Replace '24 cells'/'16 cells'/'4-substrate'/'4x6'/'4x4' in horserace.tex with the actual 30-cell / 5-substrate framing; fix robustness_battery.py:5-9 and figA_robustness_battery.py:5 docstrings to read 5 substrates x 6 outcomes.

verdict.reasoning:
All cited lines exist verbatim and say what the reviewer claims. Current "5-substrate/30-cell/5!=120" framing: horserace.tex:51 ("all $5!=120$ substrate orderings", "the thirty substrate-by-outcome tests"), :55 ("the resulting thirty substrate-by-outcome cells"), :408 and :192 (5!=120), :308/:322 ("the 30-cell matrix"), :49/:204 (five substrates). Stale legacy "4-substrate" framing: :262 ("principal 4-substrate-by-6-outcome mediation matrix"), :289 fig caption ("4-substrate-by-6-outcome value matrix"), :298 ("With 24 substrate-by-outcome mediation cells, family-wise error-rate (FWER) correction is essential"), :527 ("the ranking of substrates across the 24 cells is unchanged" + footnote "original 4x4 horserace... for the 16 cells. Extending that exercise to the 4x6 matrix"). The :51 abstract ("thirty") directly contradicts :298 ("24") on the FWER denominator within the same paper.

Code docstrings confirmed stale: robustness_battery.py:5-9 reads "All checks run on the 4-substrate x 6-outcome matrix:" and lists climate bundle, H_pred_pwadj, ancestral_yield_log, pandemic_intensity_norm — but SUBSTRATES_FOR_SHAPLEY at line 47 is the 5-set [climate_bundle, functional_alleles, neolithic_frac, ancestral_yield_log, pandemic_intensity_norm] with no H_pred. WY function docstring at line 205 also still says "24-cell mediation matrix", and line 118 has a stale cosmetic counter total = len(OUTCOMES) * 4. figA_robustness_battery.py:5 reads "4-substrate x 4-outcome heatmap".

Parquet evidence reproduced exactly: exercise1_shapley_results = 30 rows, 5 substrates; exercise2_mediation_results = 30 rows, 5 substrates; robustness_battery wy_correction check = 30 rows = 6 outcomes x 5 substrates.

Load-bearing claim verified in code: check_wy_correction (lines 214-217) builds cells over OUTCOMES x _substrate_cells() = 6x5 = 30, and line 241 sets max_F_perm[p] = max(perm_F) over all 30 cells — so the actual FWER maximization denominator is 30, not the 24 stated at horserace.tex:298. The reviewer's central point (the stated correction denominator 24 contradicts the code's 30) is true.

One nuance: because the WY permutation physically maximizes over the 30 cells regardless of the prose, the FWER protection is in fact exact and no reported statistic (the five surviving cells, F-values, p_WY) is wrong. The defect is descriptive/reproducibility: the wrong denominator is stated to the reader, and a reproducer following the docstrings would build a 4-substrate matrix including H_pred instead of the 5-substrate matrix with neolithic_frac and functional_alleles.

horserace.title: Abstract says Neolithic-ancestry fraction 'dominates' cumulative density 2025, but the Shapley table shows functional_alleles dominant on log_popd_2025
horserace.problem: The abstract states 'The agricultural-Neolithic ancestry fraction dominates the cumulative density margin and the demographic-transition timing.' Under the Shapley R^2 metric used for every other headline substrate, neolithic_frac is NOT the dominant substrate on either outcome: functional_alleles dominates log_popd_2025 (0.0641 vs 0.0390) and dt_timing_year (0.1219 vs 0.0317). The neolithic_frac claim holds only under the WY F-test metric, which is not the criterion the abstract uses for the other channels.
horserace.evidence: exercise1_shapley_results.parquet log_popd_2025 column: functional_alleles 0.0641 > neolithic_frac 0.0390 > ... ancestral_yield_log 0.0002. dt_timing_year column: functional_alleles 0.1219 > neolithic_frac 0.0317. (Largest-substrate-per-outcome printout: log_popd_2025 -> functional_alleles; dt_timing_year -> functional_alleles.)
horserace.why_it_matters: The 'temporal partition' headline is stated in Shapley-dominance terms for climate, crop yield, and functional alleles; switching silently to an F-test criterion for the neolithic_frac cells makes the partition look cleaner than the Shapley decomposition supports.
horserace.suggested_fix: State explicitly which metric (Shapley R^2 vs WY F-stat) assigns dominance for each headline cell, or soften to 'is the leading FWER-surviving substrate on cumulative density and DT timing' rather than 'dominates'.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced every cited number and the underlying logic. The abstract (horserace.tex:29) and intro (line 49) both claim "the agricultural-Neolithic ancestry fraction dominates the cumulative density margin [2025] and the demographic-transition timing." The Shapley R^2 parquet (/Volumes/BIGDATA/HYDE35/analysis/data/deep_determinants/exercise1_shapley_results.parquet) shows functional_alleles is the largest substrate on BOTH cells, not neolithic_frac: log_popd_2025 = functional_alleles 0.0641 > neolithic_frac 0.0390; dt_timing_year = functional_alleles 0.1219 > neolithic_frac 0.0317. The code's own "Largest substrate per outcome" idxmax printout (exercise1_shapley.py:229-233) therefore returns functional_alleles for both outcomes. The abstract states the OTHER headline channels strictly in Shapley terms (climate "dominates" 1500 = Shapley 0.088 largest, line 222; functional alleles "dominate" GDPpc2015 = Shapley 0.175 largest, line 218), so the reviewer's central charge — that the neolithic_frac claim silently switches to a different criterion — holds.

The criterion that does rank neolithic_frac first is the Westfall-Young Shapley F-test in robustness_battery.parquet (wy_correction rows): on log_popd_2025 neolithic_frac F=17.86, p_adj_wy=0.000 (largest F, ancestral_yield F=10.40 p=0.030, functional_alleles F=3.59 p=0.692 does not survive); on dt_timing_year neolithic_frac F=13.21 p_adj_wy=0.005 (largest, functional_alleles F=7.03 p=0.143 does not survive). So neolithic_frac genuinely is the dominant/only-surviving substrate on both cells under the WY F-test — exactly as the reviewer said.

The problem is in fact sharper than the reviewer stated. (1) The body at line 220 contains an outright false Shapley parenthetical: "Its Shapley R^2 is 0.039 on log population density 2025 (the largest substrate contribution on this outcome)" — functional_alleles 0.0641 is larger, so this is not a switch of criterion but a factual error. (2) The body at line 218 directly contradicts the abstract on dt_timing: "The functional-allele bundle dominates ... demographic-transition timing ... it contributes 0.122, also the largest," while the abstract assigns dt_timing dominance to neolithic_frac. This is an internal abstract/body inconsistency, not just opaque criterion choice.

One reviewer error, in the project's favor: the reviewer's "evidence" that the WY survivors are "ancestral crop yield (3 cells) and predicted heterozygosity (2 cells)" comes from line 298, which describes the MEDIATION WY F-test (24 cells, includes predicted heterozygosity as a substrate), a different exercise from the 30-cell Shapley-decomposition WY F-test in robustness_battery.parquet where neolithic_frac is the top survivor on these two outcomes. The reviewer conflated the two WY tests, but this error understates rather than overstates the issue, so it does not weaken the finding.
verdict.correction: The finding is correct and if anything understated. The abstract's "neolithic_frac dominates cumulative density (2025) and demographic-transition timing" is not the Shapley-dominant cell (functional_alleles wins both: 0.0641>0.0390 and 0.1219>0.0317) but is the WY F-test top survivor on both (F=17.86,p=0.000 and F=13.21,p=0.005). Beyond the criterion switch the reviewer flagged, (a) body line 220 makes a false Shapley statement — neolithic_frac's 0.039 is called "the largest substrate contribution on log_popd_2025" when functional_alleles' 0.0641 is larger — and (b) body line 218 directly contradicts the abstract by stating functional alleles are "the largest" on demographic-transition timing. Recommend either restating the abstract claim explicitly on the WY-survival criterion, or correcting the false "largest" parenthetical at line 220 and reconciling line 218 with the abstract. Note: the reviewer's secondary claim that the WY survivors are ancestral-yield/predicted-heterozygosity is from the separate mediation WY test (line 298) and is irrelevant here.

horserace.title: No reproduction entry point (no Makefile / run_all / reproduce script) and dependency order is implicit
horserace.problem: There is no orchestrator running the build_*.py layer scripts -> build_horserace_panel.py -> exercise1_shapley/exercise2_mediation -> robustness_battery -> fig*.py in dependency order. build_horserace_panel.py consumes 8 upstream parquets that must exist first, and exercise2/robustness import constants from exercise1_shapley, so order matters but is undocumented.
horserace.evidence: Globbing 'reproduce* run_all* pipeline* Makefile *.sh' in analysis/paper5_horserace returned no matches; grep for 'reproduce|run_all|pipeline' in *.py found nothing. README.md (analysis/data/deep_determinants/) documents the five data layers and the panel path but gives no build/run ordering. The companion project ships reproduce_long_shadow.sh (git log fb127eb).
horserace.why_it_matters: Without an entry point a third party must reverse-engineer the DAG; combined with the non-deterministic seeds (hr-hash-seed-nonrepro) even correct ordering will not reproduce the committed CIs.
horserace.suggested_fix: Add reproduce_horserace.sh mirroring reproduce_long_shadow.sh, running build_*.py then build_horserace_panel.py then exercise1/exercise2/robustness then fig*.py with PYTHONHASHSEED fixed, and reference it in the README.

verdict.reasoning: Tried to refute but every claim holds. (1) No orchestrator: glob for *.sh/Makefile/run_all*/reproduce*/pipeline* in /Volumes/BIGDATA/HYDE35/analysis/paper5_horserace/ returns no matches (zsh 'no matches found' + ls failures); recursive find for .sh/makefile/reproduce* returns nothing; grep -rEl 'reproduce|run_all|pipeline' *.py returns nothing. (2) Upstream parquet count: build_horserace_panel.py reads 10 distinct parquets via pd.read_parquet (lines 24-78); of these exactly 8 are produced by sibling build_*.py scripts in the same dir (predicted_het, state_history, ancestral_crop_yield, pandemic, modern_outcomes, functional_alleles, neolithic_fraction, climate_pathways), the other 2 being shared climate inputs — so 'consumes 8 upstream parquets that must exist first' is accurate. (3) Import dependency: exercise2_mediation.py:19, exercise2_subsample_stability.py:23, robustness_battery.py:28 all do 'from analysis.paper5_horserace.exercise1_shapley import (CLIMATE_BUNDLE, FUNCTIONAL_BUNDLE, OUTCOMES, CONTROLS)' — exactly the 'import constants from exercise1_shapley' the reviewer describes; five other modules import from it too. (4) README at analysis/data/deep_determinants/README.md lists substrate parquets and the panel path but gives zero build/run ordering; it is also stale ('Five substrate-layer parquets' while the build now consumes 7 from that dir), which strengthens the under-documentation point. (5) The companion reproduce_long_shadow.sh genuinely exists (at analysis/paper4_shadow/long_shadow_fertility/, slightly different path than the reviewer guessed, matching git fb127eb). Nuance: the cross-module imports are import-time (exercise1_shapley's main() is __name__-guarded so importing it does not run the Shapley computation), so the binding runtime ordering constraint is the parquet data products (deep_determinants_horserace.parquet and exercise1_shapley_results.parquet), not the constant imports per se — but this does not weaken the finding, it just clarifies the mechanism. Severity 'minor' is correct: a reproducibility/documentation gap, not a correctness defect; individual scripts run standalone.

horserace.title: Tests smoke-test output shape but never assert the WY survivor set or any paper number, so the H_pred drift went undetected
horserace.problem: The output-level tests assert only shape/existence/CI-ordering and the Shapley efficiency identity; none asserts which cells survive WY, that the substrate set excludes H_pred, or any number that appears in the paper. There is no test on robustness_battery.parquet at all. As a result the stale 'Predicted heterozygosity carries the remaining two' prose and the 24-vs-30 mismatch were never caught.

Every component of the finding checks out against the cited sources.

DIRECTORY: /Volumes/BIGDATA/HYDE35/analysis/paper5_horserace/tests/ contains 10 test files; there is NO test_robustness_battery.py, even though robustness_battery.py exists and writes analysis/data/deep_determinants/robustness_battery.parquet (190 rows, includes the wy_correction cells with p_adj_wy/f_obs). grep over tests/ for "robustness_battery" returns nothing.

CRITICAL CONFIRMATION OF THE UNDETECTED DRIFT: I loaded the three output parquets. exercise1_shapley_results, exercise2_mediation_results, and robustness_battery ALL have substrate set = {ancestral_yield_log, climate_bundle, functional_alleles, neolithic_frac, pandemic_intensity_norm}. Yet horserace.tex line 298 states "Predicted heterozygosity carries the remaining two" WY survivors (claiming F=11.33 on GDPpc 2015, F=10.82 on pop growth). The actual WY survivors from robustness_battery.parquet (p_adj_wy<0.05) are: ancestral_yield_log->log_popd_1500 (F=15.55,p=.002), ancestral_yield_log->log_popd_2025 (F=10.40,p=.030), ancestral_yield_log->log_pop_growth (F=26.97,p=.000), neolithic_frac->log_popd_2025 (F=17.86,p=.000), neolithic_frac->dt_timing_year (F=13.21,p=.005). So the two non-ancestral-yield survivors are neolithic_frac, NOT predicted heterozygosity, and the H_pred F-stats in the prose correspond to no cell in the data. NO GUARD EXISTS: grep over tests/ shows no assertion of substrate VALUES in any exercise output (only column existence + row count), no reference to p_adj_wy/f_obs/survivor counts, and no test that H_pred is absent from outputs. Neither touches the exercise outputs. So the reviewer's "why it matters" claim holds: a single assertion pinning the survivor set to the five named cells, or that no H_pred column appears in any exercise output, would have flagged the regression.
